section_summary: These pages document Japan’s tightening foreign exchange controls in 1940 and their effects on American exporters, travelers, banks, and investors. Much of the section follows The Paraffine Companies’ attempt to sell its interest in a Japanese roofing company while obtaining permission to remit the proceeds in dollars. The final documents consider how Americans leaving Japan might protect their property and convert their yen holdings.

subfiles.title: Bates International Bag Company request for assistance with Japanese remittances
subfiles.to: Department of State, attention Maxwell M. Hamilton
subfiles.about: The company seeks help collecting payments owed by Japanese associates.
subfiles.summary: Only part of its 1938 receivables had been remitted, leaving approximately $98,000 outstanding.

subfiles.title: Reply to Bates International Bag Company
subfiles.about: The Department explains the Ambassador’s authority to assist with frozen commercial debt.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton says the Ambassador in Tokyo has standing instructions to seek exchange for frozen commercial debts and will take appropriate informal action.

subfiles.title: Exchange resources of Japan at the end of 1939
subfiles.about: Points to a memorandum filed elsewhere on Japan’s exchange resources.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to file 894.51/656.

subfiles.title: Advisability of shipments on open account to Japan
subfiles.about: The consul general assesses payment risks for American shipments to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Foreign exchange controls make open-account sales risky. The despatch advises strong payment guarantees and warns that even yen deposits or settlement in Japanese goods may be difficult to convert or export.

subfiles.title: Effects of falling sterling on Japanese trade
subfiles.about: Tokyo reports concern over sterling’s decline and Japanese exchange policy.
subfiles.summary: Falling sterling harms Japanese exports and complicates imports; Japan considers fixing a preferred sterling rate.

subfiles.title: Comment on Japan’s gold shipments and cotton imports
subfiles.about: The division cautions against reading lower gold exports as an improved Japanese trade position.
subfiles.summary: Large quantities of cotton, much of it American, are held on Japanese docks without exchange permits. The memorandum suggests that shortages of foreign exchange may explain lower imports and gold shipments.

subfiles.title: Present foreign exchange position of Japan
subfiles.about: The memorandum analyzes Japan’s trade deficits, gold holdings, and reliance on sterling receipts.
subfiles.summary: Japan’s deficit with countries outside the yen bloc rose in early 1940, although its bilateral deficit with the United States fell. Estimated gold holdings were about $123 million at the end of April. Discounted sterling and prospective British clearing agreements threatened Japan’s ability to settle dollar debts.

subfiles.title: Notice to passport holders on Japanese monetary restrictions
subfiles.about: Suggests adding Asian monetary restrictions to a passport notice.
subfiles.summary: Recommends mentioning Japanese restrictions in the next revision of the traveler notice.

subfiles.title: Application of Japanese foreign exchange regulations to American travelers
subfiles.about: Summarizes Japanese limits on funds carried out by travelers and proposes advance notice to Americans.
subfiles.summary: Travelers generally needed permission to depart with funds exceeding ¥500, though letters of credit brought from abroad were exempt. Because permission could take days, the memorandum recommends informing passport applicants before departure.

subfiles.title: Application of Japanese foreign exchange control regulations to American travelers in Japan
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Embassy forwards its inquiry and Japan’s reply concerning travelers’ funds.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 4746 transmits two diplomatic notes and circulates them to American consulates under Tokyo’s supervision.

subfiles.title: American Embassy inquiry on travelers’ funds
subfiles.about: Requests authoritative guidance on the treatment of funds carried by American visitors.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy asks whether tourists and commercial travelers need permits to take out money brought from abroad and whether checks, letters of credit, drafts, and currency receive different treatment.

subfiles.title: Japanese Foreign Ministry reply on travelers’ funds
subfiles.about: States the Japanese rules for foreigners carrying travel funds out of Japan.
subfiles.summary: A foreign traveler may generally depart with up to ¥500 without permission, regardless of funds brought on entry. Larger amounts require approval, but a letter of credit issued abroad and brought into Japan may be carried out without a permit.

subfiles.title: Ordinance based upon the Foreign Exchange Control Law
subfiles.about: Provides the ordinance provisions cited in the Foreign Ministry’s reply.
subfiles.summary: The extract lists transactions requiring Finance Ministry permission and rules for carrying currency, drafts, and letters of credit abroad. It includes exceptions for limited travel expenses and specified commercial or official purposes.

subfiles.title: Paraffine Companies request for telephone consultation
subfiles.from: R. S. Shainwald and W. H. Lowe
subfiles.about: Requests a call about the company’s interest in a Japanese manufacturing plant.
subfiles.summary: The company asks Grady to discuss an urgent ownership problem.

subfiles.title: Paraffine Companies follow-up to telephone conversation
subfiles.about: Encloses the company’s account of its problem and a cable to Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Shainwald thanks Grady and asks for news of the Embassy’s response.

subfiles.title: Statement for telephone conversation with Henry F. Grady
subfiles.about: Explains the threatened loss of the company’s Japanese roofing plant interest.
subfiles.summary: Japanese shareholders seek to buy the American interest, while dollar exchange permits appear unavailable.

subfiles.title: Cable to Tokyo representatives about Embassy assistance
subfiles.about: Directs representatives to explain the ownership dispute to the American Embassy.
subfiles.summary: The company says the Department will request an Embassy report.

subfiles.title: Conversation with R. S. Shainwald on foreign-controlled companies in Japan
subfiles.about: Records Shainwald’s account of pressure to sell the American interest in Sakuma Company.
subfiles.summary: Shainwald says Japanese shareholders want the American stake and that military orders depend on Japanese ownership. A proposed sale cannot readily yield dollars because exchange permits are unavailable. Grady suggests presenting the matter to the Embassy and promises a Department inquiry.

subfiles.title: Inquiry to Tokyo about the Paraffine Companies case
subfiles.about: Requests an Embassy report and possible advice on the proposed sale.
subfiles.summary: The Department outlines the reported pressure on American shareholders and asks Tokyo for facts and suggestions.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Paraffine Companies information
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the company’s report and the Department’s request for an Embassy inquiry.
subfiles.summary: The Department has asked Tokyo for a report and possible action.

subfiles.title: Embassy report on the Sakuma Company dispute
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports the proposed sale, denial of dollar exchange, and military pressure on Sakuma Company.
subfiles.summary: Military orders sustained the company, and Japanese authorities pressed for a transfer of American shares. The Finance Ministry denied a dollar exchange permit, reportedly as part of a general refusal to permit repatriation of foreign capital. Military authorities then threatened materials and orders unless a yen sale was completed; the Embassy saw no clear discrimination but deplored the pressure.

subfiles.title: Department advice to R. S. Shainwald
subfiles.about: Explains the limited assistance available if the company decides to sell.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy may informally seek a dollar exchange permit for sale proceeds.

subfiles.title: Instructions to Embassy on Sakuma Company
subfiles.about: Directs informal assistance and further inquiry into possible duress.
subfiles.summary: If the owners sell, the Embassy should informally seek dollar exchange. It should also verify reported military threats and gather information about pressure to sell.

subfiles.title: Embassy acknowledgment of Sakuma instructions
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Confirms action on the Department’s instructions.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy expects an early Japanese reply.

subfiles.title: Grady routing note on Paraffine telegrams
subfiles.about: Requests draft replies concerning Shainwald’s message and Tokyo’s report.
subfiles.summary: Grady asks Ballantine to draft necessary telegrams.

subfiles.title: Shainwald reports deadline for Japanese share purchase
subfiles.about: Reports a deadline and threatened cancellation of orders and materials.
subfiles.summary: Shainwald seeks urgent advice after Tokyo representatives report pressure to accept yen.

subfiles.title: Confirmation of Shainwald’s urgent telegram
subfiles.about: Repeats the company’s report of Japanese pressure and request for advice.
subfiles.summary: The letter confirms the telegram warning of withdrawn materials and threatened order cancellations.

subfiles.title: Paraffine board decision to require dollar payment
subfiles.about: Reports the board’s terms for disposing of its Japanese interest.
subfiles.summary: The board will sell only if ¥600,000 is paid in American dollars.

subfiles.title: Extension of Sakuma negotiations
subfiles.about: Relays a Tokyo message granting more time for negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Representatives report an extension until the following Wednesday and expect a Foreign Office reply.

subfiles.title: Grady’s update to Shainwald
subfiles.about: Responds to the board’s decision and reports on Embassy efforts.
subfiles.summary: Grady acknowledges the dollar-payment condition and negotiation extension, and indicates that the Embassy has approached Japanese authorities.

subfiles.title: Shanghai financing agreement and exchange questions
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram on proposed American financing of Japanese undertakings in China.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Shanghai telegram 883 in file 894.51/679.

subfiles.title: Embassy follow-up on the Paraffine Companies case
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports the Japanese response and continuing Sakuma operations.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Office had not replied to Embassy inquiries, and the War Department reportedly rebuked Sakuma’s managing director for seeking help. Despite earlier threats, the company continued receiving materials and orders. The Embassy recommends no further action until coercion or refusal of exchange after a completed sale can be shown.

subfiles.title: Grady’s assessment of the Sakuma case
subfiles.about: Explains why further Embassy action is not yet warranted.
subfiles.summary: Although military authorities threatened Sakuma in August, the company continued to receive orders and materials. Grady says the Embassy needs evidence of forced sale or a refused permit after sale before taking further action.

subfiles.title: Shainwald reports restrictions on auditing and foreign management
subfiles.about: Forwards Tokyo representatives’ reports on pressure affecting Sakuma Company.
subfiles.summary: Authorities barred audits and restricted Alexander’s presence at the office. Representatives reported a general refusal of permits to repatriate foreign capital, conditional military business, and reduced railway orders linked to foreign ownership. Shainwald also relayed an example of pressure on a Canadian educator in Japan.

subfiles.title: National City Bank report on Shanghai exchange controls
subfiles.from: National City Bank of New York
subfiles.about: Forwards a Shanghai cable about prospective Japanese trade controls.
subfiles.summary: The cable reports proposed export controls and a requirement to sell exchange to Yokohama Specie Bank.

subfiles.title: Hamilton’s reply to National City Bank
subfiles.to: National City Bank of New York
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the bank’s report on Japanese measures in Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton welcomes cooperative action by foreign banks resisting Japanese trade and financial controls.

subfiles.title: Routing request for reply to Shainwald
subfiles.about: Requests a reply to Shainwald during Grady’s absence.
subfiles.summary: The reply should pass through A-G and be returned for Grady’s review.

subfiles.title: Attempt to remit sale proceeds through canned crab trade
subfiles.about: Reports a failed proposal to turn yen sale proceeds into dollars through crab exports.
subfiles.summary: A proposed canned crab transaction was rejected; negotiations and raw material supplies continued temporarily.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Shainwald’s August and September letters
subfiles.about: Acknowledges further reports while Grady is away.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton says the Department has no additional information and will pass further news to Shainwald.

subfiles.title: Alexander’s report on Embassy contacts and military pressure
subfiles.about: Forwards extracts from Alexander’s account of Embassy contacts and pressure from Japanese authorities.
subfiles.summary: Alexander describes contact with Embassy officer Crocker, military objections to his presence at Sakuma’s office, and efforts to find another means of remittance.

subfiles.title: Request to acknowledge Shainwald’s letter
subfiles.about: Requests an acknowledgment for Grady’s signature.
subfiles.summary: The note asks Coville to prepare the reply before Grady returns.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Shainwald’s September letter
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the company’s further report on its Japanese interests.
subfiles.summary: Brief acknowledgment of Shainwald’s letter.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about exchange for departing Americans
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Seeks guidance on converting departing Americans’ Japanese assets into foreign exchange.
subfiles.summary: Grew advises formal applications before considering remedies for refused permits and asks for Department comment.

subfiles.title: Department approval of advice to Yokohama consul
subfiles.about: Approves Grew’s response to the consul at Yokohama.
subfiles.summary: The Department requests reports of significant developments.

subfiles.title: Instructions on American withdrawals and property inventories
subfiles.about: Gives guidance on exchange difficulties and inventories for Americans leaving East Asia.
subfiles.summary: The Department asks the Embassy to monitor exchange difficulties and assist affected Americans. It prefers no general inventory instruction but will supply guidance for Americans who inquire.

subfiles.title: British plans for exchange and property inventories in Japan
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports British plans for stranded yen funds and inventories and asks for American guidance.
subfiles.summary: British officials considered delaying Japanese transfers within the British Empire to bargain for release of British nationals’ yen, and considered limited Embassy deposits for evacuees. They also instructed British subjects to inventory their possessions. Americans asked whether they should do likewise, prompting Grew to request Department instructions.

subfiles.title: Policy memorandum on inventories and exchange assistance
subfiles.about: Explains the policy basis for the draft instructions to Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Individual inventory advice and Embassy help converting evacuees’ liquid assets are considered consistent with past practice.
